text: {"entries":[{"name_han":"广列仙传","logic_thesis":"The text proves that immortality is not a closed mythic past but a continuous, verifiable human career: once the conditions of virtue, timing, and method are met, the same outcome reappears across ages. By expanding earlier immortals’ lists, it argues that the Daoist path is empirically accumulative—more cases strengthen the law, not dilute it. Immortality is therefore a repeatable causal pattern, not a unique miracle.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Early immortal biographies already show patterned outcomes under patterned practices. 2. Expanding the corpus multiplies independent instances of the same pattern. 3. If many independent cases converge, the outcome is law-like rather than anecdotal. 4. Law-like outcomes imply transferable conditions (virtue, technique, karmic timing). 5. Therefore later aspirants can reason from precedent rather than from revelation alone. 6. Conclusion: Immortality is historically demonstrable and pedagogically usable.","logic_practice":"1. Treat immortal stories as case-law: extract the repeated causal factors (virtue, mountain retreat, timing, master transmission). 2. Map those factors onto a BaZi chart’s favorable elements and career/health pillars as ‘conditions of readiness.’ 3. Use biography clusters of the same deity/lineage as evidence of method stability when choosing a cultivation style. 4. Reject one-off marvels that lack transferable premises. 5. Build a personal ‘precedent file’: which historical paths match your day-master temperament and resource environment.","logic_compare":"Unlike pure hagiographic praise collections, 广列仙传 argues by accumulation of cases, closer to inductive historiography than to devotion. It differs from 列仙传 by scale and continuity: expansion itself is the proof strategy. Where 仙佛奇踪 mixes Buddhist–Daoist wonder for entertainment, this text’s logic is serial confirmation of a Daoist career law."},{"name_han":"历代神仙通鉴","logic_thesis":"It proves that sacred history can be synchronized: gods, emperors, and cosmic cycles form one continuous timeline in which spiritual rank is a function of historical position and moral-cosmic office. Immortality is not outside chronology; it is the upper register of the same causal order that governs dynasties. The text’s ‘mirror’ logic claims that reading history correctly reveals the hierarchy of the unseen.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Human history and divine offices occur in one temporal field. 2. If the same calendar can host both, ranking rules must be shared or at least commensurate. 3. Synchronizing reigns, revelations, and apotheoses yields a single chain of cause and succession. 4. Breaks in virtue or mandate appear as falls; alignments appear as elevation or theophany. 5. Therefore spiritual status is historically legible, not purely mystical. 6. Conclusion: Cosmology is a readable chronicle, and cultivation is entry into that chronicle’s higher offices.","logic_practice":"1. Read your life years against larger sexagenary and dynastic-style cycles (大运 as ‘reign periods’ of the self). 2. Treat BaZi luck pillars as office-shifts: when qi aligns with mandate, advance practice; when not, consolidate virtue. 3. Use historical immortal ‘appointment’ stories as models for vocation timing, not only for techniques. 4. Diagnose setbacks as mandate-mismatch before blaming method alone. 5. Keep a personal chronicle linking events, virtue work, and chart periods.","logic_compare":"Unlike 广列仙传’s inductive case pile, 通鉴 forces a total timeline—its proof is systemic synchronization. It is more ‘state historiography of Heaven’ than local mountain gazetteer. Compared with 三教源流搜神大全, it privileges chronological integration over encyclopedic deity taxonomy."},{"name_han":"八仙得道传","logic_thesis":"The novel proves that diverse social types can complete the same Dao if each converts its dominant flaw and talent under correct guidance and ordeal. Attainment is not class-bound: the path is universal, but the alchemy is personal. Group immortality further proves that mutual aid and complementary natures are themselves a method, not a side-plot.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Eight different temperaments and stations all face conversion to the Dao. 2. Each succeeds only after a trial that targets that temperament’s specific obstruction. 3. Shared teaching plus differentiated ordeal implies a two-layer law: universal principle, particular medicine. 4. Their later ensemble function shows complementarity as a higher-order technique. 5. Therefore ‘one Dao, many entries’ is not relativism but calibrated causality. 6. Conclusion: Cultivation success is personalized transformation within a collective field.","logic_practice":"1. Identify your ‘Eight Immortals type’ by BaZi day-master and strong/weak stars (which flaw is structural). 2. Design practice around that flaw (e.g., greed → generosity regimen; rigidity → softness training). 3. Prefer teacher–peer circles over lone grinding when your chart shows weak resource/output. 4. Treat setbacks as prescribed ordeal matching the chart’s clash/harm, not random bad luck. 5. Use group ritual or shared study as intentional complementarity when solo methods stall.","logic_compare":"Unlike 七真因果传, which centers Quanzhen historical lineage and karmic accounting, 八仙得道传 is typological romance proving social pluralism of the path. It is less institutional than 长春道教源流 and less doctrinal than 净明宗教录; its logic is character-alchemy through narrative trial."},{"name_han":"七真因果传","logic_thesis":"It proves that Daoist perfection is inseparable from causal retribution and prior vows: the Seven Perfected attain not by technique alone but by paying and transforming karmic debt under Wang Chongyang’s restructuring of life. The ‘cause–effect biography’ form itself argues that spiritual rank is an ethical-karmic equation solved in history.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Each of the Seven carries distinct past causes and worldly bonds. 2. Conversion scenes reframe those bonds as fuel or obstacle under new vows. 3. Suffering, renunciation, and discipline appear as payment and purification of causes. 4. Collective success under one master shows lineage as a karmic technology, not mere school branding. 5. Therefore attainment is measurable as transformed cause–effect, not only as mystical state. 6. Conclusion: True cultivation is ethical–karmic engineering within a transmission.","logic_practice":"1. Audit life patterns that repeat (relationship, money, health) as BaZi-visible ‘causes’ before adding methods. 2. Pair technical practice with concrete vow-and-repair acts (restitution, service, restraint). 3. Use clash years as repayment windows: intensify ethical repair rather than only defensive talismans. 4. Prefer lineage accountability (teacher, community) if your chart shows weak self-control stars. 5. Track progress by cessation of old causal loops, not by peak experiences alone.","logic_compare":"It differs from 八仙得道传 by grounding fiction in Quanzhen historical persons and explicit karma accounting. Versus 长春道教源流, it argues through narrative causality rather than documentary lineage. Against purely method books like 万法归宗, it insists ethics and debt are first-order, not prefaces."},{"name_han":"三教源流搜神大全","logic_thesis":"The encyclopedia proves that the sacred pantheon is a governed ecology: each deity’s office, origin story, and cult domain can be classified, so efficacy depends on correct jurisdictional invocation. Syncretism is not confusion; it is a mapped division of labor among Confucian, Buddhist, and Daoist powers. Knowing ‘who does what’ is itself a logical condition of successful request.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: The three teachings generate overlapping but not identical sacred offices. 2. Tracing origins assigns jurisdiction and proper ritual address. 3. Misaddressed petition fails because office, not sincerity alone, channels response. 4. Classification therefore predicts which spirit answers which class of problem. 5. Hence religious practice is administrative correctness under Heaven’s bureaucracy. 6. Conclusion: Encyclopedic knowledge is operational power, not scholastic ornament.","logic_practice":"1. Match petition type to deity office (career, plague, exam, household) rather than to popularity. 2. Align request timing with BaZi favorable elements and the deity’s traditional calendrical days. 3. Avoid stacking conflicting cults when chart already shows authority conflict (官杀混杂 analogy). 4. Use origin stories to decide whether a spirit is local, celestial, or underworld before ritual design. 5. Keep a personal ‘office map’ for recurring life domains.","logic_compare":"Unlike 历代神仙通鉴’s continuous chronicle, this work’s logic is taxonomic and practical. It is broader than pure Daoist hagiography and less skeptical than 集说诠真. Compared with 铸鼎余闻’s critical notes, 搜神大全 assumes pantheon validity and optimizes navigation."},{"name_han":"太上灵宝净明宗教录","logic_thesis":"It proves that the highest Daoist method collapses into luminous loyalty and heart-rectification: outer rites without 净明 (pure illumination) of intent are structurally invalid. The Jingming school argues that social virtue (忠孝) is not a lower Confucian substitute for alchemy but the efficient cause of spiritual clarity. Doctrine is thus ethical luminosity operationalized as religion.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Ritual and register systems aim at communion with the pure. 2. Impure motive contaminates the same channels the rite opens. 3. Therefore purification of loyalty/filiality/intent is prior to technical elaboration. 4. If virtue produces 明, then social ethics are soteriological technology. 5. Lineage records exist to stabilize this priority against method fetishism. 6. Conclusion: True Lingbao efficacy is moral–cognitive purity under form, not form alone.","logic_practice":"1. Before any talisman/ritual day indicated by BaZi, run a motive audit (gain, revenge, fear, service). 2. Use 忠孝-style concrete acts as pre-ritual ‘fire purification’ of intent. 3. Prefer simple correct form over complex wrong-hearted technique when chart shows strong killing/authority pressure. 4. Measure practice by clarity and reduced self-deception, not only by omens. 5. In teaching or self-work, rank ethical modules above acquisition of secret methods.","logic_compare":"It differs from 灵验符咒全书 and 万法归宗 by demoting technique to secondary status. Against theatrical immortal novels, its proof is institutional-ethical, not narrative wonder. Relative to Quanzhen sources, Jingming foregrounds Confucian-coded loyalty as Daoist soteriology rather than full monastic renunciation."},{"name_han":"龙虎山志","logic_thesis":"The gazetteer proves that sacred power is place-bound and institutionally continuous: Longhu Mountain’s geography, lineage of Heavenly Masters, and ritual monopoly form a single causal system. Orthodoxy is not only doctrinal correctness but territorial–genealogical custody of registers and methods. Landscape, lineage, and law co-produce legitimacy.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Zhengyi authority claims descent and mountain seat. 2. Recording terrain, temples, and successive masters ties efficacy to a locatable institution. 3. If rites work through registers held by that line, then place and pedigree are causal, not decorative. 4. Local history thus functions as proof of transmission integrity. 5. Breaks in place/lineage predict ritual illegitimacy. 6. Conclusion: Daoist power is a geo-institutional technology.","logic_practice":"1. When choosing Zhengyi-style practice, privilege verified transmission over anonymous ‘secret books.’ 2. Treat sacred mountains as amplifiers: plan major vows/retreats when BaZi travel/resource stars support mountain work. 3. Map your ‘home altar’ as a micro-territory—clean jurisdiction before complex rites. 4. Use lineage calendars and mountain feast days as external clocks alongside personal luck pillars. 5. Diagnose failed rites for transmission or place error before blaming destiny alone.","logic_compare":"Unlike generic immortal biographies, 龙虎山志 argues from site + institution. Compared with 罗浮山志会编 or 洞霄图志, it specifically defends Heavenly Master orthodoxy rather than general mountain sanctity. Versus method manuals, it proves custody, not recipe."},{"name_han":"灵验符咒全书","logic_thesis":"It proves that ritual language and diagram are causal instruments: when form, timing, breath, and deity alignment are correct, results are expected as law, not as favor. ‘Efficacy’ (灵验) is the empirical criterion—methods survive by reported success, creating a pragmatic epistemology of the occult. The book’s completeness claim implies that technique space is finite and classifiable.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Specific graphs/sounds correspond to specific spirit-functions. 2. Correct performance couples human qi, cosmic timing, and that function. 3. Repeated efficacy reports inductively validate the coupling. 4. Failures are reassigned to error in form/timing/purity, preserving the law. 5. Therefore the sacred is experimentally addressable through standardized tools. 6. Conclusion: Occult practice is a craft epistemology under cosmological assumptions.","logic_practice":"1. Never use a talisman without matching problem-class, deity, and electional timing (BaZi hour/day selection). 2. Train breath, writing order, and material as one chain—partial form equals null method. 3. Log outcomes like experiments: conditions, chart day, result, to refine personal efficacy. 4. Pair with purity rules from Jingming-type ethics to avoid ‘valid form, toxic intent.’ 5. Start with few high-confidence methods rather than collecting volumes.","logic_compare":"Unlike 净明宗教录, this text’s primary proof is pragmatic efficacy, not moral ontology. It is more applied than mountain gazetteers and less narrative than immortal novels. Compared with 万法归宗, it is closer to a working grimoire of results than to a philosophical unification of methods."},{"name_han":"有象列仙全传","logic_thesis":"It proves that visual form is a legitimate channel of recognition and transmission: the immortal is knowable by image as well as by text, so iconography stabilizes identity across time. Seeing and reading together reduce ambiguity about who is cultivated and how they appear in the religious imagination. Embodiment in portrait is an argument that the path leaves readable signs.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Names alone drift; portraits fix attributes and narrative markers. 2. Fixed attributes allow cross-text identification of the same figure. 3. Identification enables correct cult, meditation visualization, and lineage memory. 4. Thus image is not ornament but epistemic control on sacred persons. 5. A complete illustrated series claims comprehensive coverage of models. 6. Conclusion: Visualization accuracy is part of doctrinal accuracy.","logic_practice":"1. Use stable iconographic traits in 存思/visualization so the mind locks a consistent deity form. 2. Match chosen immortal models to BaZi temperament (e.g., martial vs. literary types) for resonance. 3. Prefer illustrated hagiographies when teaching beginners to reduce name confusion. 4. Inspect altar images for attribute consistency with the office you petition. 5. Treat dream/vision appearances against classical image standards before accepting them as guidance.","logic_compare":"Unlike text-only 广列仙传, 有象 makes likeness itself a proof technology. It is less chronological-systemic than 历代神仙通鉴 and less critical than 铸鼎余闻. Relative to 仙佛奇踪, it stays within immortal portrait-logic rather than mixed wonder anthology."},{"name_han":"仙佛奇踪","logic_thesis":"It proves by juxtaposition that ‘strange traces’ of immortals and Buddhas inhabit one marvel continuum: extraordinary biography is a shared religious rhetoric across Daoism and Buddhism. The anthology logic claims that wonder authenticates sanctity more than sectarian boundary does. Crossing traditions becomes evidence of a common upper path expressed in different costumes.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Both traditions preserve wonder-working biographies. 2. Placing them together reveals isomorphic structures (renunciation, power, compassion, liberation). 3. Isomorphism suggests a shared grammar of sanctity beyond institutional labels. 4. Readers are trained to recognize the pattern rather than police borders. 5. Therefore ‘odd traces’ function as comparative proof of transcendence. 6. Conclusion: Syncretic reading is a method for discerning the real path under forms.","logic_practice":"1. When your chart shows mixed cultural/religious influences, use comparative models instead of forced purity anxiety. 2. Extract shared cultivation moves (detachment, discipline, compassion) as core, treat sect dress as secondary. 3. Use marvel stories cautiously as inspiration, then demand ethical and practical tests. 4. In BaZi counseling, translate ‘奇’ events as strong spirit/clash activations needing grounding practice. 5. Avoid collecting wonders as spiritual consumerism; map each to a training principle.","logic_compare":"Unlike 三教源流搜神大全’s administrative taxonomy, 仙佛奇踪 persuades by aesthetic–narrative juxtaposition. It is lighter and more literary than 长春道教源流’s documentary Quanzhen history. Versus skeptical 集说诠真, it assumes marvels as positive data."},{"name_han":"长春道教源流","logic_thesis":"It proves that Quanzhen’s authority is genealogical and historical: the path’s truth is secured by documented origin, master–disciple chains, and institutional memory centered on Qiu Changchun’s line. Legitimacy is a historical argument—without source continuity, claims of method collapse. Daoism here is a reconstructible river, not a free marketplace of techniques.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Authentic teaching requires traceable transmission. 2. Compiling origins and branches reconstructs the river from source to streams. 3. Where documents and lineage cohere, doctrine is trustworthy. 4. Where they break, later inventions are downgraded. 5. Therefore historiography is a purity filter for practice. 6. Conclusion: Cultivation choice should follow evidenced lineage, not fashion.","logic_practice":"1. Before adopting ‘Quanzhen’ labels, check whether your methods match documented lineage concerns (celibacy, interior alchemy priorities, communal rule). 2. Use BaZi teacher-luck (印星) periods to seek authentic instruction rather than random books. 3. Prefer source-near practices when chart shows confusion from too many inputs (食伤过旺 analogy). 4. Keep a transmission notebook: who taught what, when, under what conditions. 5. Treat historical crises of the school as warnings about state, travel, and patronage timing.","logic_compare":"Unlike 七真因果传’s karmic storytelling, this text proves by documentary genealogy. It is narrower and more confessional than universal immortal anthologies. Compared with 龙虎山志, it argues Northern Quanzhen continuity rather than Zhengyi mountain-register orthodoxy."},{"name_han":"白云仙表","logic_thesis":"It proves that the White Cloud institutional milieu can tabulate and present immortal/master identities as a structured gallery of models—sanctity is teachable by exemplar tables, not only by secret oral lore. Ordering figures into a ‘table’ argues that the path has a curriculum of persons: ranks, roles, and exempla you can locate yourself against. Identity lists become a pedagogical logic.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Communities need stable rosters of who counts as model and ancestor. 2. Tabulation fixes names, titles, and relationships. 3. Fixed rosters enable ritual remembrance and imitation hierarchies. 4. Imitation hierarchies convert vague aspiration into role-based practice. 5. Therefore institutional memory produces cultivational clarity. 6. Conclusion: Knowing the table of exemplars is part of knowing the Way.","logic_practice":"1. Build a personal ‘仙表’: 3–5 exemplars matching your BaZi strengths/weaknesses. 2. Assign each exemplar a training module (stillness, service, study, martial qi). 3. Use memorial days of those figures as checkpoints in your luck cycles. 4. In temple or home cult, recite roster to stabilize intention and reduce random deity shopping. 5. Update the table as your chart periods shift emphasis (e.g., from study印 to action伤官).","logic_compare":"More institutional-roster than free hagiographic expansion like 广列仙传. Less cosmic-chronological than 历代神仙通鉴 and less critical-philological than 铸鼎余闻. Compared with 长春道教源流, it functions as exemplar display for White Cloud context rather than full origin treatise."},{"name_han":"秘传万法归宗","logic_thesis":"It proves that the multiplicity of spells, arts, and schools is apparent, not ultimate: all methods return to one ancestral principle (宗), so mastery is unification under root law rather than hoarding branches. Secrecy frames the claim that only those who grasp the root may safely operate the branches. The book’s architecture is a monist argument disguised as a toolbox.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Methods proliferate and seem mutually foreign. 2. If they work in one cosmos, they must share generative principles (qi, mind, spirit, correspondence). 3. Tracing branches back yields a root grammar. 4. Operating branches without root produces unstable or harmful results. 5. Therefore true transmission is root-first, technique-second. 6. Conclusion: ‘Myriad methods’ are one method refracted.","logic_practice":"1. For any new technique, write its root principle in one sentence before practice. 2. Use BaZi to see which root you naturally access (water stillness, fire refinement, metal cutting, etc.) and specialize before diversifying. 3. Cull redundant methods that do not increase root clarity. 4. In conflict years, return to root practices (breath, virtue, simple rite) over exotic additions. 5. Test ‘secret’ claims by whether they illuminate the root or only multiply steps.","logic_compare":"Unlike 灵验符咒全书’s empirical catalog, 万法归宗 insists on metaphysical reunification. It is more synoptic than Jingming’s ethical purity thesis and more technical than pure lineage histories. Against encyclopedic 神异典, it is a practitioner’s monism, not an imperial classification of marvels."},{"name_han":"逍遥山万寿宫通志","logic_thesis":"It proves that a temple complex and its mountain form a complete sacred polity: ritual life, local history, endowments, and immortal associations cohere into one living system of efficacy. The palace is not a building but a continuous argument that place-based institutional Daoism sustains the path in the world. Local gazetteer completeness equals proof of durability.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Wanshou Palace’s rites, lands, and stories persist together. 2. Recording them binds spiritual claim to socioeconomic and geographic fact. 3. Persistence under change implies institutional resilience as a form of verification. 4. Local immortal ties further root universal Dao in particular soil. 5. Therefore cultivation affiliated with such a center inherits structured support. 6. Conclusion: Temple–mountain systems are engines of long-horizon practice.","logic_practice":"1. Anchor practice to a real temple calendar when possible—external structure corrects chart chaos. 2. Time pilgrimages or major vows to BaZi support for travel and noble helpers (贵人). 3. Study the temple’s resident deities’ offices before making petitions. 4. Contribute service/resources as participation in the ‘polity,’ not only as transaction. 5. Treat local temple history as case studies of how communities survive bad cycles.","logic_compare":"Like other mountain gazetteers but centered on palace institution at Xiaoyao rather than Zhengyi Longhu monopoly or Luofu’s broader multi-lineage sanctity. Less about personal alchemy narrative, more about corporate sacred continuity. Differs from novelistic immortal tales by evidentiary local documentation."},{"name_han":"罗浮山志会编","logic_thesis":"It proves by compilation that Luofu’s sanctity is multi-source and layered: earlier records, immortals, herbs, and hermits accumulate into a mountain that teaches through environment as much as through text. The ‘会编’ method argues that truth about a sacred site is distributed across sources and must be recombined. Nature, lore, and practice form one pedagogical ecology.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: No single prior account exhausts Luofu. 2. Compiling variants and domains (geo, bio, hagiographic) yields a fuller causal picture. 3. Mountain efficacy appears as the intersection of place qi, historical practice, and narrative memory. 4. Therefore the site is a composite teacher. 5. Practitioners reason from layers, not from one legend. 6. Conclusion: Sacred geography is an edited archive of living forces.","logic_practice":"1. Read multi-source mountain records before retreat to know which micro-sites match your aim (alchemy, healing, seclusion). 2. Align retreat timing with BaZi seasonal needs (e.g., wood/fire support vs. water excess). 3. Use herbal/local knowledge as embodied five-phase training, not tourism. 4. Compare conflicting legends to extract stable practice motifs. 5. After retreat, log environmental effects on mind/qi as data for future site choice.","logic_compare":"More compilatory and nature-inclusive than 龙虎山志’s institutional Zhengyi focus. Broader than a single-temple 通志. Versus purely biographical immortal books, it elevates landscape as co-author of attainment."},{"name_han":"洞霄图志","logic_thesis":"It proves that diagram and gazetteer together make a sacred site cognitively operable: maps, images, and records convert Dongxiao from vague holiness into navigable structure. Spatial representation is an argument that correct movement, dwelling, and ritual placement matter. To know the plan is to know how the mountain works.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Sacred sites have internal topology of halls, peaks, and paths. 2. Illustration fixes that topology for memory and pilgrimage. 3. Coupled text explains function of each node. 4. Correct use of nodes (where to stay, offer, cultivate) follows from the plan. 5. Therefore cartographic knowledge is ritual competence. 6. Conclusion: Sacred space is a diagram of practice.","logic_practice":"1. Before any sacred-site visit, study layout: approach path as purification sequence. 2. Place home altar with analogous spatial logic (clear hierarchy, left/right functions). 3. Use BaZi directionology sparingly but consistently with site topology, not against it. 4. Practice walking meditation as reading the mountain’s diagram with the body. 5. Sketch your own practice space ‘图志’ to expose clutter and broken hierarchy.","logic_compare":"More explicitly visual-spatial than prose-only gazetteers. Unlike 有象列仙全传’s person portraits, it diagrams place. Compared with imperial 神异典, it is local and operational rather than encyclopedic-categorical."},{"name_han":"铸鼎余闻","logic_thesis":"It proves that popular god-lore must be smelted: leftover notes after ‘casting the tripod’ of research show that careful collation and residual problems are how truth is refined from rumor. The scholarly remainder is an argument against naive acceptance—what cannot be fused cleanly remains as critical heat. Religious knowledge advances by philological fire.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Cult stories and names are inconsistent across sources. 2. Comparative sifting separates stable ore from slag. 3. Residues and doubts are retained rather than forced smooth. 4. Retained problems prevent false certainty in practice and history. 5. Therefore critical leftover is epistemic virtue. 6. Conclusion: Mature belief includes documented uncertainty.","logic_practice":"1. When a BaZi/spirit claim is popular, demand at least two independent classical witnesses. 2. Keep a ‘余闻’ file of unresolved deity/method contradictions instead of fake reconciliation. 3. Do not base high-stakes rites on single late novelistic sources. 4. Use critical reading years (strong 印) to clean your belief system. 5. Teach juniors the difference between liturgical usefulness and historical certainty.","logic_compare":"Opposite spirit to marvel anthologies like 仙佛奇踪; closer to 集说诠真’s critical stance but as residual scholarly notes rather than systematic debunking. Differs from gazetteers that legitimize sites; it pressure-tests lore itself."},{"name_han":"集说诠真","logic_thesis":"It proves that collecting sayings is only valuable if subordinated to ‘clarifying the true’: syncretic or popular claims must be judged against a standard of authenticity, often exposing excess, contradiction, or non-classical accretion. The logic is adjudicative—truth is what survives cross-examination. Religious speech is evidence to be weighed, not merely treasured.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Many schools and tales assert conflicting sacred facts. 2. Gathering them without a criterion multiplies error. 3. Applying a truth standard (sources, coherence, moral/cosmological fitness) filters claims. 4. Surviving claims gain higher warrant; rejected ones free practice from noise. 5. Therefore discernment is the master method above accumulation. 6. Conclusion: Clarification is a form of salvation from false paths.","logic_practice":"1. Install a personal criterion set (classical warrant, ethical non-harm, testability, lineage) before adding practices. 2. Quarterly review: drop methods that fail criteria even if emotionally appealing. 3. In BaZi consultation, separate symbolic language from causal overclaim. 4. Prefer fewer verified operations in 灵验 work. 5. Use debate/writing to force clarity—unwritable claims are suspect.","logic_compare":"More systematically adjudicative than 铸鼎余闻’s residual notes. Antithetical to 灵验符咒全书’s collect-and-use pragmatism unless efficacy is strictly tested. Unlike 三教搜神大全, it does not assume the pantheon’s operational map is self-justifying."},{"name_han":"古今图书集成·神异典","logic_thesis":"The imperial encyclopedia proves that the strange is a classifiable department of knowledge: marvels, spirits, and anomalies can be ordered under leishu logic for state and scholar use. Classification itself is the argument—chaos of reports becomes administrative and intellectual order. Cosmic oddities are thereby integrated into the same knowledge empire as politics and nature.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Records of the strange are vast and scattered. 2. Imperial compilation assigns categories and parallel entries. 3. Categorization enables comparison, retrieval, and pattern recognition. 4. Patterns suggest regularities even inside anomaly. 5. Therefore the supernatural is not outside knowledge but a section of it. 6. Conclusion: Ordered wonder supports reasoned governance of belief and research.","logic_practice":"1. File personal omens/events into categories (dream, illness, object, landscape) before interpreting via BaZi. 2. Compare your case against class analogs rather than unique panic readings. 3. Use encyclopedia-style breadth to avoid single-school tunnel vision. 4. For research cultivation, build a leishu of techniques by function. 5. Let classification cool emotional contagion from ‘神异’ experiences.","logic_compare":"Scale and neutrality differ from confessional Daoist lineage books; it is bibliocratic, not sectarian. Unlike 夷坚志’s narrative miscellany voice, 神异典 aims at systematic placement. Versus 集说诠真, compilation precedes judgment—order first, critique optional."},{"name_han":"夷坚志","logic_thesis":"Hong Mai’s collection proves that anomaly reports, gathered at scale from contemporary witnesses, form a social epistemology of the strange: recurrence across informants warrants attention even without doctrinal closure. The zhiguai method argues that Heaven’s order leaks into anecdote, and careful miscellany can register those leaks. Moral and causal patterns emerge from many small cases rather than from system first.","logic_chain":"1. Premise: Individuals report encounters with ghosts, retribution, and marvels. 2. Independent reports with similar structures reduce pure invention probability. 3. Embedded moral outcomes suggest ethical causality in ordinary life. 4. The compiler’s breadth substitutes for controlled experiment. 5. Therefore narrative data is usable evidence for cosmic-moral law. 6. Conclusion: The strange is socially witnessed regularity, not only elite revelation.","logic_practice":"1. Treat client anecdotes in BaZi work as data points: look for repeated retribution/timing motifs. 2. Correlate reported hauntings or omens with clash/harm/void configurations before ritual escalation. 3. Extract ethical lessons (greed, betrayal, filial breach) as primary interventions. 4. Keep a modern 夷坚-style log of verified odd events tied to charts. 5. Resist over-systematizing a single story; wait for pattern across cases.","logic_compare":"Unlike imperial 神异典, it is authorial miscellany with literary immediacy, not bureaucratic classification. Unlike Daoist institutional gazetteers, it is largely non-sectarian social reporting. Compared with immortal hagiography, it foregrounds ordinary people under causal law more than career transcendence."}]}

Let me research these texts carefully to produce accurate scholarly content about...I can help you extract logical reasoning from those classical Chinese BaZi/Daoist texts and return structured JSON. However, I need to clarify something first: the texts you listed are primarily hagiographies and gazetteers of Daoist immortals, not core BaZi/Daoist philosophical treatises.

entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that immortality is not a closed mythic past but a continuous, verifiable human career: once the conditions of virtue, timing, and method are met, the same outcome reappears across ages. By expanding earlier immortals’ lists, it argues that the Daoist path is empirically accumulative—more cases strengthen the law, not dilute it. Immortality is therefore a repeatable causal pattern, not a unique miracle.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Early immortal biographies already show patterned outcomes under patterned practices. 2. Expanding the corpus multiplies independent instances of the same pattern. 3. If many independent cases converge, the outcome is law-like rather than anecdotal. 4. Law-like outcomes imply transferable conditions (virtue, technique, karmic timing). 5. Therefore later aspirants can reason from precedent rather than from revelation alone. 6. Conclusion: Immortality is historically demonstrable and pedagogically usable.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Treat immortal stories as case-law: extract the repeated causal factors (virtue, mountain retreat, timing, master transmission). 2. Map those factors onto a BaZi chart’s favorable elements and career/health pillars as ‘conditions of readiness.’ 3. Use biography clusters of the same deity/lineage as evidence of method stability when choosing a cultivation style. 4. Reject one-off marvels that lack transferable premises. 5. Build a personal ‘precedent file’: which historical paths match your day-master temperament and resource environment.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure hagiographic praise collections, 广列仙传 argues by accumulation of cases, closer to inductive historiography than to devotion. It differs from 列仙传 by scale and continuity: expansion itself is the proof strategy. Where 仙佛奇踪 mixes Buddhist–Daoist wonder for entertainment, this text’s logic is serial confirmation of a Daoist career law.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that sacred history can be synchronized: gods, emperors, and cosmic cycles form one continuous timeline in which spiritual rank is a function of historical position and moral-cosmic office. Immortality is not outside chronology; it is the upper register of the same causal order that governs dynasties. The text’s ‘mirror’ logic claims that reading history correctly reveals the hierarchy of the unseen.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Human history and divine offices occur in one temporal field. 2. If the same calendar can host both, ranking rules must be shared or at least commensurate. 3. Synchronizing reigns, revelations, and apotheoses yields a single chain of cause and succession. 4. Breaks in virtue or mandate appear as falls; alignments appear as elevation or theophany. 5. Therefore spiritual status is historically legible, not purely mystical. 6. Conclusion: Cosmology is a readable chronicle, and cultivation is entry into that chronicle’s higher offices.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Read your life years against larger sexagenary and dynastic-style cycles (大运 as ‘reign periods’ of the self). 2. Treat BaZi luck pillars as office-shifts: when qi aligns with mandate, advance practice; when not, consolidate virtue. 3. Use historical immortal ‘appointment’ stories as models for vocation timing, not only for techniques. 4. Diagnose setbacks as mandate-mismatch before blaming method alone. 5. Keep a personal chronicle linking events, virtue work, and chart periods.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 广列仙传’s inductive case pile, 通鉴 forces a total timeline—its proof is systemic synchronization. It is more ‘state historiography of Heaven’ than local mountain gazetteer. Compared with 三教源流搜神大全, it privileges chronological integration over encyclopedic deity taxonomy.

entries.logic_thesis: The novel proves that diverse social types can complete the same Dao if each converts its dominant flaw and talent under correct guidance and ordeal. Attainment is not class-bound: the path is universal, but the alchemy is personal. Group immortality further proves that mutual aid and complementary natures are themselves a method, not a side-plot.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Eight different temperaments and stations all face conversion to the Dao. 2. Each succeeds only after a trial that targets that temperament’s specific obstruction. 3. Shared teaching plus differentiated ordeal implies a two-layer law: universal principle, particular medicine. 4. Their later ensemble function shows complementarity as a higher-order technique. 5. Therefore ‘one Dao, many entries’ is not relativism but calibrated causality. 6. Conclusion: Cultivation success is personalized transformation within a collective field.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Identify your ‘Eight Immortals type’ by BaZi day-master and strong/weak stars (which flaw is structural). 2. Design practice around that flaw (e.g., greed → generosity regimen; rigidity → softness training). 3. Prefer teacher–peer circles over lone grinding when your chart shows weak resource/output. 4. Treat setbacks as prescribed ordeal matching the chart’s clash/harm, not random bad luck. 5. Use group ritual or shared study as intentional complementarity when solo methods stall.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 七真因果传, which centers Quanzhen historical lineage and karmic accounting, 八仙得道传 is typological romance proving social pluralism of the path. It is less institutional than 长春道教源流 and less doctrinal than 净明宗教录; its logic is character-alchemy through narrative trial.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that Daoist perfection is inseparable from causal retribution and prior vows: the Seven Perfected attain not by technique alone but by paying and transforming karmic debt under Wang Chongyang’s restructuring of life. The ‘cause–effect biography’ form itself argues that spiritual rank is an ethical-karmic equation solved in history.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Each of the Seven carries distinct past causes and worldly bonds. 2. Conversion scenes reframe those bonds as fuel or obstacle under new vows. 3. Suffering, renunciation, and discipline appear as payment and purification of causes. 4. Collective success under one master shows lineage as a karmic technology, not mere school branding. 5. Therefore attainment is measurable as transformed cause–effect, not only as mystical state. 6. Conclusion: True cultivation is ethical–karmic engineering within a transmission.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Audit life patterns that repeat (relationship, money, health) as BaZi-visible ‘causes’ before adding methods. 2. Pair technical practice with concrete vow-and-repair acts (restitution, service, restraint). 3. Use clash years as repayment windows: intensify ethical repair rather than only defensive talismans. 4. Prefer lineage accountability (teacher, community) if your chart shows weak self-control stars. 5. Track progress by cessation of old causal loops, not by peak experiences alone.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from 八仙得道传 by grounding fiction in Quanzhen historical persons and explicit karma accounting. Versus 长春道教源流, it argues through narrative causality rather than documentary lineage. Against purely method books like 万法归宗, it insists ethics and debt are first-order, not prefaces.

entries.logic_thesis: The encyclopedia proves that the sacred pantheon is a governed ecology: each deity’s office, origin story, and cult domain can be classified, so efficacy depends on correct jurisdictional invocation. Syncretism is not confusion; it is a mapped division of labor among Confucian, Buddhist, and Daoist powers. Knowing ‘who does what’ is itself a logical condition of successful request.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: The three teachings generate overlapping but not identical sacred offices. 2. Tracing origins assigns jurisdiction and proper ritual address. 3. Misaddressed petition fails because office, not sincerity alone, channels response. 4. Classification therefore predicts which spirit answers which class of problem. 5. Hence religious practice is administrative correctness under Heaven’s bureaucracy. 6. Conclusion: Encyclopedic knowledge is operational power, not scholastic ornament.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Match petition type to deity office (career, plague, exam, household) rather than to popularity. 2. Align request timing with BaZi favorable elements and the deity’s traditional calendrical days. 3. Avoid stacking conflicting cults when chart already shows authority conflict (官杀混杂 analogy). 4. Use origin stories to decide whether a spirit is local, celestial, or underworld before ritual design. 5. Keep a personal ‘office map’ for recurring life domains.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 历代神仙通鉴’s continuous chronicle, this work’s logic is taxonomic and practical. It is broader than pure Daoist hagiography and less skeptical than 集说诠真. Compared with 铸鼎余闻’s critical notes, 搜神大全 assumes pantheon validity and optimizes navigation.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the highest Daoist method collapses into luminous loyalty and heart-rectification: outer rites without 净明 (pure illumination) of intent are structurally invalid. The Jingming school argues that social virtue (忠孝) is not a lower Confucian substitute for alchemy but the efficient cause of spiritual clarity. Doctrine is thus ethical luminosity operationalized as religion.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Ritual and register systems aim at communion with the pure. 2. Impure motive contaminates the same channels the rite opens. 3. Therefore purification of loyalty/filiality/intent is prior to technical elaboration. 4. If virtue produces 明, then social ethics are soteriological technology. 5. Lineage records exist to stabilize this priority against method fetishism. 6. Conclusion: True Lingbao efficacy is moral–cognitive purity under form, not form alone.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Before any talisman/ritual day indicated by BaZi, run a motive audit (gain, revenge, fear, service). 2. Use 忠孝-style concrete acts as pre-ritual ‘fire purification’ of intent. 3. Prefer simple correct form over complex wrong-hearted technique when chart shows strong killing/authority pressure. 4. Measure practice by clarity and reduced self-deception, not only by omens. 5. In teaching or self-work, rank ethical modules above acquisition of secret methods.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from 灵验符咒全书 and 万法归宗 by demoting technique to secondary status. Against theatrical immortal novels, its proof is institutional-ethical, not narrative wonder. Relative to Quanzhen sources, Jingming foregrounds Confucian-coded loyalty as Daoist soteriology rather than full monastic renunciation.

entries.logic_thesis: The gazetteer proves that sacred power is place-bound and institutionally continuous: Longhu Mountain’s geography, lineage of Heavenly Masters, and ritual monopoly form a single causal system. Orthodoxy is not only doctrinal correctness but territorial–genealogical custody of registers and methods. Landscape, lineage, and law co-produce legitimacy.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Zhengyi authority claims descent and mountain seat. 2. Recording terrain, temples, and successive masters ties efficacy to a locatable institution. 3. If rites work through registers held by that line, then place and pedigree are causal, not decorative. 4. Local history thus functions as proof of transmission integrity. 5. Breaks in place/lineage predict ritual illegitimacy. 6. Conclusion: Daoist power is a geo-institutional technology.
entries.logic_practice: 1. When choosing Zhengyi-style practice, privilege verified transmission over anonymous ‘secret books.’ 2. Treat sacred mountains as amplifiers: plan major vows/retreats when BaZi travel/resource stars support mountain work. 3. Map your ‘home altar’ as a micro-territory—clean jurisdiction before complex rites. 4. Use lineage calendars and mountain feast days as external clocks alongside personal luck pillars. 5. Diagnose failed rites for transmission or place error before blaming destiny alone.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike generic immortal biographies, 龙虎山志 argues from site + institution. Compared with 罗浮山志会编 or 洞霄图志, it specifically defends Heavenly Master orthodoxy rather than general mountain sanctity. Versus method manuals, it proves custody, not recipe.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that ritual language and diagram are causal instruments: when form, timing, breath, and deity alignment are correct, results are expected as law, not as favor. ‘Efficacy’ (灵验) is the empirical criterion—methods survive by reported success, creating a pragmatic epistemology of the occult. The book’s completeness claim implies that technique space is finite and classifiable.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Specific graphs/sounds correspond to specific spirit-functions. 2. Correct performance couples human qi, cosmic timing, and that function. 3. Repeated efficacy reports inductively validate the coupling. 4. Failures are reassigned to error in form/timing/purity, preserving the law. 5. Therefore the sacred is experimentally addressable through standardized tools. 6. Conclusion: Occult practice is a craft epistemology under cosmological assumptions.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Never use a talisman without matching problem-class, deity, and electional timing (BaZi hour/day selection). 2. Train breath, writing order, and material as one chain—partial form equals null method. 3. Log outcomes like experiments: conditions, chart day, result, to refine personal efficacy. 4. Pair with purity rules from Jingming-type ethics to avoid ‘valid form, toxic intent.’ 5. Start with few high-confidence methods rather than collecting volumes.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 净明宗教录, this text’s primary proof is pragmatic efficacy, not moral ontology. It is more applied than mountain gazetteers and less narrative than immortal novels. Compared with 万法归宗, it is closer to a working grimoire of results than to a philosophical unification of methods.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that visual form is a legitimate channel of recognition and transmission: the immortal is knowable by image as well as by text, so iconography stabilizes identity across time. Seeing and reading together reduce ambiguity about who is cultivated and how they appear in the religious imagination. Embodiment in portrait is an argument that the path leaves readable signs.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Names alone drift; portraits fix attributes and narrative markers. 2. Fixed attributes allow cross-text identification of the same figure. 3. Identification enables correct cult, meditation visualization, and lineage memory. 4. Thus image is not ornament but epistemic control on sacred persons. 5. A complete illustrated series claims comprehensive coverage of models. 6. Conclusion: Visualization accuracy is part of doctrinal accuracy.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Use stable iconographic traits in 存思/visualization so the mind locks a consistent deity form. 2. Match chosen immortal models to BaZi temperament (e.g., martial vs. literary types) for resonance. 3. Prefer illustrated hagiographies when teaching beginners to reduce name confusion. 4. Inspect altar images for attribute consistency with the office you petition. 5. Treat dream/vision appearances against classical image standards before accepting them as guidance.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike text-only 广列仙传, 有象 makes likeness itself a proof technology. It is less chronological-systemic than 历代神仙通鉴 and less critical than 铸鼎余闻. Relative to 仙佛奇踪, it stays within immortal portrait-logic rather than mixed wonder anthology.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves by juxtaposition that ‘strange traces’ of immortals and Buddhas inhabit one marvel continuum: extraordinary biography is a shared religious rhetoric across Daoism and Buddhism. The anthology logic claims that wonder authenticates sanctity more than sectarian boundary does. Crossing traditions becomes evidence of a common upper path expressed in different costumes.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Both traditions preserve wonder-working biographies. 2. Placing them together reveals isomorphic structures (renunciation, power, compassion, liberation). 3. Isomorphism suggests a shared grammar of sanctity beyond institutional labels. 4. Readers are trained to recognize the pattern rather than police borders. 5. Therefore ‘odd traces’ function as comparative proof of transcendence. 6. Conclusion: Syncretic reading is a method for discerning the real path under forms.
entries.logic_practice: 1. When your chart shows mixed cultural/religious influences, use comparative models instead of forced purity anxiety. 2. Extract shared cultivation moves (detachment, discipline, compassion) as core, treat sect dress as secondary. 3. Use marvel stories cautiously as inspiration, then demand ethical and practical tests. 4. In BaZi counseling, translate ‘奇’ events as strong spirit/clash activations needing grounding practice. 5. Avoid collecting wonders as spiritual consumerism; map each to a training principle.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 三教源流搜神大全’s administrative taxonomy, 仙佛奇踪 persuades by aesthetic–narrative juxtaposition. It is lighter and more literary than 长春道教源流’s documentary Quanzhen history. Versus skeptical 集说诠真, it assumes marvels as positive data.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that Quanzhen’s authority is genealogical and historical: the path’s truth is secured by documented origin, master–disciple chains, and institutional memory centered on Qiu Changchun’s line. Legitimacy is a historical argument—without source continuity, claims of method collapse. Daoism here is a reconstructible river, not a free marketplace of techniques.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Authentic teaching requires traceable transmission. 2. Compiling origins and branches reconstructs the river from source to streams. 3. Where documents and lineage cohere, doctrine is trustworthy. 4. Where they break, later inventions are downgraded. 5. Therefore historiography is a purity filter for practice. 6. Conclusion: Cultivation choice should follow evidenced lineage, not fashion.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Before adopting ‘Quanzhen’ labels, check whether your methods match documented lineage concerns (celibacy, interior alchemy priorities, communal rule). 2. Use BaZi teacher-luck (印星) periods to seek authentic instruction rather than random books. 3. Prefer source-near practices when chart shows confusion from too many inputs (食伤过旺 analogy). 4. Keep a transmission notebook: who taught what, when, under what conditions. 5. Treat historical crises of the school as warnings about state, travel, and patronage timing.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 七真因果传’s karmic storytelling, this text proves by documentary genealogy. It is narrower and more confessional than universal immortal anthologies. Compared with 龙虎山志, it argues Northern Quanzhen continuity rather than Zhengyi mountain-register orthodoxy.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the White Cloud institutional milieu can tabulate and present immortal/master identities as a structured gallery of models—sanctity is teachable by exemplar tables, not only by secret oral lore. Ordering figures into a ‘table’ argues that the path has a curriculum of persons: ranks, roles, and exempla you can locate yourself against. Identity lists become a pedagogical logic.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Communities need stable rosters of who counts as model and ancestor. 2. Tabulation fixes names, titles, and relationships. 3. Fixed rosters enable ritual remembrance and imitation hierarchies. 4. Imitation hierarchies convert vague aspiration into role-based practice. 5. Therefore institutional memory produces cultivational clarity. 6. Conclusion: Knowing the table of exemplars is part of knowing the Way.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Build a personal ‘仙表’: 3–5 exemplars matching your BaZi strengths/weaknesses. 2. Assign each exemplar a training module (stillness, service, study, martial qi). 3. Use memorial days of those figures as checkpoints in your luck cycles. 4. In temple or home cult, recite roster to stabilize intention and reduce random deity shopping. 5. Update the table as your chart periods shift emphasis (e.g., from study印 to action伤官).
entries.logic_compare: More institutional-roster than free hagiographic expansion like 广列仙传. Less cosmic-chronological than 历代神仙通鉴 and less critical-philological than 铸鼎余闻. Compared with 长春道教源流, it functions as exemplar display for White Cloud context rather than full origin treatise.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that the multiplicity of spells, arts, and schools is apparent, not ultimate: all methods return to one ancestral principle (宗), so mastery is unification under root law rather than hoarding branches. Secrecy frames the claim that only those who grasp the root may safely operate the branches. The book’s architecture is a monist argument disguised as a toolbox.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Methods proliferate and seem mutually foreign. 2. If they work in one cosmos, they must share generative principles (qi, mind, spirit, correspondence). 3. Tracing branches back yields a root grammar. 4. Operating branches without root produces unstable or harmful results. 5. Therefore true transmission is root-first, technique-second. 6. Conclusion: ‘Myriad methods’ are one method refracted.
entries.logic_practice: 1. For any new technique, write its root principle in one sentence before practice. 2. Use BaZi to see which root you naturally access (water stillness, fire refinement, metal cutting, etc.) and specialize before diversifying. 3. Cull redundant methods that do not increase root clarity. 4. In conflict years, return to root practices (breath, virtue, simple rite) over exotic additions. 5. Test ‘secret’ claims by whether they illuminate the root or only multiply steps.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 灵验符咒全书’s empirical catalog, 万法归宗 insists on metaphysical reunification. It is more synoptic than Jingming’s ethical purity thesis and more technical than pure lineage histories. Against encyclopedic 神异典, it is a practitioner’s monism, not an imperial classification of marvels.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that a temple complex and its mountain form a complete sacred polity: ritual life, local history, endowments, and immortal associations cohere into one living system of efficacy. The palace is not a building but a continuous argument that place-based institutional Daoism sustains the path in the world. Local gazetteer completeness equals proof of durability.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Wanshou Palace’s rites, lands, and stories persist together. 2. Recording them binds spiritual claim to socioeconomic and geographic fact. 3. Persistence under change implies institutional resilience as a form of verification. 4. Local immortal ties further root universal Dao in particular soil. 5. Therefore cultivation affiliated with such a center inherits structured support. 6. Conclusion: Temple–mountain systems are engines of long-horizon practice.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Anchor practice to a real temple calendar when possible—external structure corrects chart chaos. 2. Time pilgrimages or major vows to BaZi support for travel and noble helpers (贵人). 3. Study the temple’s resident deities’ offices before making petitions. 4. Contribute service/resources as participation in the ‘polity,’ not only as transaction. 5. Treat local temple history as case studies of how communities survive bad cycles.
entries.logic_compare: Like other mountain gazetteers but centered on palace institution at Xiaoyao rather than Zhengyi Longhu monopoly or Luofu’s broader multi-lineage sanctity. Less about personal alchemy narrative, more about corporate sacred continuity. Differs from novelistic immortal tales by evidentiary local documentation.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves by compilation that Luofu’s sanctity is multi-source and layered: earlier records, immortals, herbs, and hermits accumulate into a mountain that teaches through environment as much as through text. The ‘会编’ method argues that truth about a sacred site is distributed across sources and must be recombined. Nature, lore, and practice form one pedagogical ecology.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: No single prior account exhausts Luofu. 2. Compiling variants and domains (geo, bio, hagiographic) yields a fuller causal picture. 3. Mountain efficacy appears as the intersection of place qi, historical practice, and narrative memory. 4. Therefore the site is a composite teacher. 5. Practitioners reason from layers, not from one legend. 6. Conclusion: Sacred geography is an edited archive of living forces.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Read multi-source mountain records before retreat to know which micro-sites match your aim (alchemy, healing, seclusion). 2. Align retreat timing with BaZi seasonal needs (e.g., wood/fire support vs. water excess). 3. Use herbal/local knowledge as embodied five-phase training, not tourism. 4. Compare conflicting legends to extract stable practice motifs. 5. After retreat, log environmental effects on mind/qi as data for future site choice.
entries.logic_compare: More compilatory and nature-inclusive than 龙虎山志’s institutional Zhengyi focus. Broader than a single-temple 通志. Versus purely biographical immortal books, it elevates landscape as co-author of attainment.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that diagram and gazetteer together make a sacred site cognitively operable: maps, images, and records convert Dongxiao from vague holiness into navigable structure. Spatial representation is an argument that correct movement, dwelling, and ritual placement matter. To know the plan is to know how the mountain works.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Sacred sites have internal topology of halls, peaks, and paths. 2. Illustration fixes that topology for memory and pilgrimage. 3. Coupled text explains function of each node. 4. Correct use of nodes (where to stay, offer, cultivate) follows from the plan. 5. Therefore cartographic knowledge is ritual competence. 6. Conclusion: Sacred space is a diagram of practice.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Before any sacred-site visit, study layout: approach path as purification sequence. 2. Place home altar with analogous spatial logic (clear hierarchy, left/right functions). 3. Use BaZi directionology sparingly but consistently with site topology, not against it. 4. Practice walking meditation as reading the mountain’s diagram with the body. 5. Sketch your own practice space ‘图志’ to expose clutter and broken hierarchy.
entries.logic_compare: More explicitly visual-spatial than prose-only gazetteers. Unlike 有象列仙全传’s person portraits, it diagrams place. Compared with imperial 神异典, it is local and operational rather than encyclopedic-categorical.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that popular god-lore must be smelted: leftover notes after ‘casting the tripod’ of research show that careful collation and residual problems are how truth is refined from rumor. The scholarly remainder is an argument against naive acceptance—what cannot be fused cleanly remains as critical heat. Religious knowledge advances by philological fire.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Cult stories and names are inconsistent across sources. 2. Comparative sifting separates stable ore from slag. 3. Residues and doubts are retained rather than forced smooth. 4. Retained problems prevent false certainty in practice and history. 5. Therefore critical leftover is epistemic virtue. 6. Conclusion: Mature belief includes documented uncertainty.
entries.logic_practice: 1. When a BaZi/spirit claim is popular, demand at least two independent classical witnesses. 2. Keep a ‘余闻’ file of unresolved deity/method contradictions instead of fake reconciliation. 3. Do not base high-stakes rites on single late novelistic sources. 4. Use critical reading years (strong 印) to clean your belief system. 5. Teach juniors the difference between liturgical usefulness and historical certainty.
entries.logic_compare: Opposite spirit to marvel anthologies like 仙佛奇踪; closer to 集说诠真’s critical stance but as residual scholarly notes rather than systematic debunking. Differs from gazetteers that legitimize sites; it pressure-tests lore itself.

entries.logic_thesis: It proves that collecting sayings is only valuable if subordinated to ‘clarifying the true’: syncretic or popular claims must be judged against a standard of authenticity, often exposing excess, contradiction, or non-classical accretion. The logic is adjudicative—truth is what survives cross-examination. Religious speech is evidence to be weighed, not merely treasured.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Many schools and tales assert conflicting sacred facts. 2. Gathering them without a criterion multiplies error. 3. Applying a truth standard (sources, coherence, moral/cosmological fitness) filters claims. 4. Surviving claims gain higher warrant; rejected ones free practice from noise. 5. Therefore discernment is the master method above accumulation. 6. Conclusion: Clarification is a form of salvation from false paths.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Install a personal criterion set (classical warrant, ethical non-harm, testability, lineage) before adding practices. 2. Quarterly review: drop methods that fail criteria even if emotionally appealing. 3. In BaZi consultation, separate symbolic language from causal overclaim. 4. Prefer fewer verified operations in 灵验 work. 5. Use debate/writing to force clarity—unwritable claims are suspect.
entries.logic_compare: More systematically adjudicative than 铸鼎余闻’s residual notes. Antithetical to 灵验符咒全书’s collect-and-use pragmatism unless efficacy is strictly tested. Unlike 三教搜神大全, it does not assume the pantheon’s operational map is self-justifying.

entries.logic_thesis: The imperial encyclopedia proves that the strange is a classifiable department of knowledge: marvels, spirits, and anomalies can be ordered under leishu logic for state and scholar use. Classification itself is the argument—chaos of reports becomes administrative and intellectual order. Cosmic oddities are thereby integrated into the same knowledge empire as politics and nature.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Records of the strange are vast and scattered. 2. Imperial compilation assigns categories and parallel entries. 3. Categorization enables comparison, retrieval, and pattern recognition. 4. Patterns suggest regularities even inside anomaly. 5. Therefore the supernatural is not outside knowledge but a section of it. 6. Conclusion: Ordered wonder supports reasoned governance of belief and research.
entries.logic_practice: 1. File personal omens/events into categories (dream, illness, object, landscape) before interpreting via BaZi. 2. Compare your case against class analogs rather than unique panic readings. 3. Use encyclopedia-style breadth to avoid single-school tunnel vision. 4. For research cultivation, build a leishu of techniques by function. 5. Let classification cool emotional contagion from ‘神异’ experiences.
entries.logic_compare: Scale and neutrality differ from confessional Daoist lineage books; it is bibliocratic, not sectarian. Unlike 夷坚志’s narrative miscellany voice, 神异典 aims at systematic placement. Versus 集说诠真, compilation precedes judgment—order first, critique optional.

entries.logic_thesis: Hong Mai’s collection proves that anomaly reports, gathered at scale from contemporary witnesses, form a social epistemology of the strange: recurrence across informants warrants attention even without doctrinal closure. The zhiguai method argues that Heaven’s order leaks into anecdote, and careful miscellany can register those leaks. Moral and causal patterns emerge from many small cases rather than from system first.
entries.logic_chain: 1. Premise: Individuals report encounters with ghosts, retribution, and marvels. 2. Independent reports with similar structures reduce pure invention probability. 3. Embedded moral outcomes suggest ethical causality in ordinary life. 4. The compiler’s breadth substitutes for controlled experiment. 5. Therefore narrative data is usable evidence for cosmic-moral law. 6. Conclusion: The strange is socially witnessed regularity, not only elite revelation.
entries.logic_practice: 1. Treat client anecdotes in BaZi work as data points: look for repeated retribution/timing motifs. 2. Correlate reported hauntings or omens with clash/harm/void configurations before ritual escalation. 3. Extract ethical lessons (greed, betrayal, filial breach) as primary interventions. 4. Keep a modern 夷坚-style log of verified odd events tied to charts. 5. Resist over-systematizing a single story; wait for pattern across cases.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike imperial 神异典, it is authorial miscellany with literary immediacy, not bureaucratic classification. Unlike Daoist institutional gazetteers, it is largely non-sectarian social reporting. Compared with immortal hagiography, it foregrounds ordinary people under causal law more than career transcendence.
